The post-abolition size drop — evidence file

What this file shows. After the ALS abolition (treatment = government land × apartment opens on/after 26 Feb 2016), government-land supply shifts toward smaller flats within size bands (Large+XL ≈−350 ft²***, Mid ≈−44 ft²***), its Large+XL segment stops carrying a price premium (open ≈−2,600/ft²**, robust to FE-residualization; transacted close prices agree), it sells slower on launch, and its release behaviour (PO pacing and batch sizes) shifts. The robustness section shows the size result is not driven by flat-count mandates, district composition, developer mix, buyer origin, or the Nov-2016 stamp duty. All estimates are copied unchanged from the working sketch (sketch.html); each item notes its original reference number there.

Potential tests (open items)

  1. Alternative treatment timing at FY2012/13 (‘no more auctions’). The trigger mechanism was already moribund before the formal abolition — 2 ALS-triggered sales in FY12/13 against 20 government-initiated force-sales off the List, and the government had been force-selling the List since FY10/11. If the effective regime change is FY12/13 (or earlier) rather than FY13/14, the current cutoffs mis-time treatment for part of the sample. Test: re-run the 2×2 with land-purchase timing at FY12/13+, and/or shift the apartment-opening cutoff to the first sales from FY12/13-purchased land, and compare against the 2016-02-26 baseline.
  2. The non-first-PO restriction. Rationale: the two PO controls (days since last PO, previous round’s sell-through) are undefined for a development’s first recorded round, and launch rounds are structurally different (marketing-priced, lead units). Implications to test: if the treatment changes the trajectory from launch to later rounds (price escalation, size sequencing), conditioning on non-first-PO rounds samples treated and control developments at different points of that trajectory — the first-PO-only headline variant (the figure above) is sparse by construction (one bin per development), so a pooled first-PO vs non-first-PO interaction test would be the sharper check. Clarification of the sample rule: rounds >1 that open on the same day as the previous round ARE in the non-first-PO sample (days-since-last-PO = 0, previous round’s sell-through defined) — 152 of 668 non-first-PO rounds (23%), carrying 29% of the estimation sample’s apartments, are such same-day lists, so multi-list launch days are substantially represented.
  3. Does the private-land side change composition? The mix-rotation evidence (T-tables under the headline figure) is about government land; the DiD reads the private arm as the counterfactual, so its own composition drift matters. First cut: the private-land pre/post table below the government one — compare the L|M|S share shifts across the two arms; if private rotates similarly, the government rotation is partly market-wide demand, not regime. Full characteristics comparison (size/price/developer/district) in section 7.6.

new in size_drop; land attributes from landsale.csv via the same lot/name join as the AV lookup (premium and site-area lookups added for this table); development-level split by the development's first-sale date, so each development counts once, on its ds1 side; min_flats NA = the Conditions of Sale set no flat-count clause, so 'floored' counts cover devms with a clause only; the share row splits the cell's developments' total sampled saleable ft² (their apartments in A_all, ALL size bands, not just the column's band) across L = Large+XL | M = Mid | S = Nano+Small; the units-share row repeats the same split on apartment COUNTS instead of summed ft²; the two '| floored' share rows repeat both splits restricted to the cell's FLOORED developments' apartments ('--' if the cell has no floored devms). The last two rows express the flat-count mandate as a per-flat saleable size: the uniform-size row divides each floored development's saleable-equivalent envelope (0.8 × max GFA; the 0.8 converts the GFA-based bound to saleable area per the C1 convention — saleable runs ≈75–85% of GFA) by its required flat count and averages across floored devms; the band-uniform row instead gives each floored devm the COLUMN BAND's slice of that envelope — the FLOORED-ONLY cell-aggregate ft² share of the band (unrounded fraction from the '| floored' share row) × 0.8 × max GFA, divided by the floored-only cell-aggregate unit share of the band × required flats — i.e., the per-flat size implied if the devm split its envelope and its mandated flats across bands like the cell's floored aggregate; averaged over floored devms with ≥1 sampled apartment in the column's band and a parseable max GFA ('--' if none).

new in size_drop (three tables above); counterfactual outcome: would the size drop appear if floored sites had built exactly at their permitted uniform size? Every flat in a FLOORED government development carries its development's saleable-equivalent mandated uniform size (0.8 × max GFA / required flats, a devm-level constant); private and no-floor government flats keep their actual sizes. Footnote on the factor: 0.8 converts the GFA-based bound to saleable area, per the C1 convention (saleable runs ≈75–85% of GFA). Floored developments without a parseable max GFA are dropped from these samples entirely: Large+XL 5 devms / 909 apartments; Mid 5 devms / 765 apartments; Nano+Small 7 devms / 482 apartments. Caveat: floored units carry a devm-constant outcome, so identification within floored developments comes entirely from the private/no-floor sides and from composition (which floored devms open when), not from within-devm size variation.

new in size_drop (three tables above); second counterfactual, BAND-uniform allocation: instead of one uniform size per floored development (the overall-uniform set above), the mandate envelope (0.8 × max GFA, saleable-equivalent) is first split across size bands by the period-matched FLOORED-ONLY cell-aggregate ft² shares of the govt-land characteristics table's cells (the band sample × the development's own pre/post ds1-period at 2016-02-26, shares computed over the cell's floored devms' apartments only — the '| floored' share rows of that table), and the required flat count by the matching floored-only cell-aggregate unit shares; each floored-govt flat in the band then carries size = (ft² share × 0.8 × max GFA) / (unit share × required flats), a devm × period constant. The allocation applies only to floored developments with ≥1 sampled unit in the band (automatic here: the band samples condition on units in the band); private and no-floor government flats keep their actual sizes. Floored developments without a parseable max GFA are dropped entirely, as in the overall-uniform set: Large+XL 5 devms / 909 apartments; Mid 5 devms / 765 apartments; Nano+Small 7 devms / 482 apartments. Contrast with the overall-uniform set above: there every floored devm gets one size regardless of band, so its band-sample estimates mix the mandate with the devm's band mix; here the envelope is reweighted to the band before dividing, so the comparison across the two sets shows how sensitive the counterfactual is to the allocation rule. Same identification caveat: floored units carry a devm(×period)-constant outcome.

7.5 Alternative treatment timing (first openings of FY11/12 and FY10/11 land)

The trigger mechanism decayed before the formal FY13/14 abolition — the government had been force-selling List sites from FY10/11 — so the effective regime change may predate the baseline cutoff of 26 Feb 2016 (= the first opening of FY13/14-purchased land). The two replicas below move the cutoff to the first opening of FY11/12-purchased government land (25 Jul 2014, Metro6) and of FY10/11-purchased government land (29 Apr 2013, Green Code). A pure timing shift: the treated group is unchanged (all government-land apartments opening on/after the cutoff); only the before/after split and the event-time origin move.

7.6 Private-arm stability: did private-land developments change at the cutoff?

The DiD reads the private arm as the counterfactual, so drift in who builds on private land and what they build matters directly (open item 3 completes here). Both tables split each band sample's developments by first-sale date at the cutoff, exactly as the pre/post composition tables at the top of the file (each development counts once, contributing all its band-sample apartments to its ds1 side): private-land developments first, then the government replica with identical rows as the reference — control-arm drift only matters relative to the treated arm's shift.

new in size_drop; sample = the non-first-PO band estimation samples; Top-4 = SHKP/CK/Henderson/NWD (as in section 7.3); price and size rows aggregate apartments, development rows count devms once. Caveat: raw devm-cohort splits, unadjusted — not the DiD. Verdict: the private arm is not frozen — its post-cutoff cohort is fewer, larger projects (mean apartments per development 102→161 in the Large+XL sample, 106→214 in Mid) in fewer districts (15→8; 14→9) — but on the two margins that matter for the DiD it is stable or moves against the result: the Top-4 share of private developments barely moves (45→53% / 63→55% / 53→61%), and within-band private sizes drift UP in all three bands (means 849→907, 513→532, 284→307 ft²) while the government side is flat-to-down (981→978, 530→522, 404→331). The negative Govt×Post size effects are therefore a genuine relative rotation, not an artifact of a changing control arm; the honest corollary is that the Large+XL ‘drop’ is partly the private arm moving upmarket rather than absolute government shrinkage (raw government L+XL mean is flat, though its median falls 903→844), whereas the Mid and Nano+Small compressions show in the government raw levels themselves.

new in size_drop; launch-round replicas of the two tables above: apartments restricted to each development's FIRST recorded price-offer round (po non-missing, days-since-last-PO undefined) — the complementary sample of the non-first-PO estimation samples, as in the first-PO headline figure at the top of the file. Development counts can differ from the tables above: a development enters only if its first recorded round contains apartments in the column's band (and per issue 1 in noted_issues.md the first RECORDED round is not always the true launch round where early price lists were lost).
